newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding reserves, some expect no action.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding reserves, some expect no action.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is expected to add reserves to the banking system on Wednesday via system repurchase agreements, analysts said.
Some experts said, however, the Fed might stay out of the market after a round of 14-day fixed system customer repurchase agreements it conducted on Tuesday.
Analysts at J.P. Morgan expect the Fed to add reserves via term system RPs. Pundits at consulting firm MMS International also see the Fed injecting reserves into the system via system repos.
However, Dana Saporta, economist at Stone and McCarthy Research Associates, expects the Fed to refrain from any open market operation on Wednesday.

"We're expecting the open market desk to stay out today. We think that yesterday's 14-day system RP is sufficient for today at least," Saporta said. "The Fed will stay out today and then perhaps do a few more moderate injections in the second week of the period, which begins tomorrow."
At 0925 EST/1425 GMT, federal funds traded at 5-3/16 percent, below the Fed's 5-1/4 percent target.
